memory_candidates.content: When migrating pseudocode-documentation shell logic between two markdown SKILL.md files that share test infrastructure extracting fixed-anchor text regions (e.g. an awk script matching a literal echo string and appending a synthetic 'fi'), any new conditional wrapped directly around the anchor line will leave an extra unclosed `if` at the point the extraction truncates, breaking `bash -n` on the extracted region even though the full file is fine. Fix: keep the anchor line's own echo unconditional/unchanged, and put any new mode-gated behavior in a separate, fully self-closed `if ... fi` block BEFORE it.

When porting a 'Increment cycle_count. Loop continues.' style directive from a source engine into a differently-ordered position in a target engine (e.g. moving Stage 4b's churn check to run strictly after Stage 5's own tail-end increment, to fix an ordering defect), do not port the literal increment statement verbatim — check whether the counter is already incremented exactly once elsewhere in the new position's control flow. A second literal increment silently double-charges a budget counter.
